key_insight: Mesoscale neural operators learn nonlocal constitutive laws from molecular dynamics while preserving strain energy density and fracture energy across scales.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables continuum fracture predictions on domains much larger than the atomistic training specimens.
method: Learn a nonlocal kernel and nonlinear constitutive relation from MD loading and displacement data.
Normalize the kernel to preserve strain energy density under horizon rescaling.
Rescale critical bond stretch to maintain consistent energy release rates.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests recovered the nonlocal model; MD-based tests matched energy metrics within 3% and out-of-distribution peak forces within 6%, with fracture branching demonstrated on a plate 4000 times the training-specimen area.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported tests; transfer to other materials and loading regimes requires further evaluation.
paper_title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
